newsitem.title: USA: Boeing seen at beginning of order cycle.
newsitem.headline: Boeing seen at beginning of order cycle.

text.p: Boeing Co commercial aircraft group President Ron Woodard said on Thursday that he thought the manufacturer was still at the beginning of a "fairly major" airline industry order cycle.

"We've still got a lot of big carriers with substantial requirements," Woodard told reporters after announcing a sale of at least $6.5 billion worth of aircraft to AMR Corp's American Airlines, which he called one of the most significant in the company's history.

So far this year, Boeing has announced orders for 618 jets valued at $45.45 billion, compared with 346 jets worth $31.2 billion in all of last year. But Woodard said he did not think the cycle had peaked.

"The airlines' profitability continues to improve, the world economy is good and I think we're at the beginning of a fairly major cycle," Woodard said. "It looks good for as far as we can see with our crystal ball."
Woodard said the latest deal was particularly important because Boeing won the right to be the exclusive supplier of new aircraft to American, the nation's No. 2 airline, from mid-1998 through 2018.
He said the order was expected to amount to about 630 planes, or one out of every 20 the company plans to build.
"This is going to give us a sustained production base for 20 years," Woodard said.
He said he did not see any current need to increase production rates to meet the demand posed by the latest order.
